label: 1. Find one
title: Find the patient who supplied this ID
explanation: The database compares the supplied ID and finds Dana. Ordinary columns are returned; national_id is NULL. The application can use the identifier without reading the stored value.
next: The same column privilege also lets ordinary SQL read the whole column. Try ‘Read IDs’.

notes: PROTECTED column patients.national_id is matched by equality through the blind index of MATCH DOMAIN person_id.
Output column national_id is PROTECTED column patients.national_id (MATCH DOMAIN person_id) and is returned as NULL.

label: 2. Read IDs
title: Try to retrieve every stored identifier
explanation: With direct SELECT access, regular SQL returns all six stored IDs. DEP returns six NULLs. Removing the WHERE clause does not turn permission to match into permission to read identifiers.
next: NULL protects the output. It does not remove the rows or make other returned fields anonymous.

notes: Output column national_id is PROTECTED column patients.national_id (MATCH DOMAIN person_id) and is returned as NULL.

label: 3. Join one
title: Connect one patient to their medical records
sql:
SELECT p.full_name, m.diagnosis
FROM patients AS p
JOIN medical_records AS m
  ON m.patient_national_id = p.national_id
WHERE p.national_id = '123456782';
explanation: Both queries return Dana’s diagnoses. DEP permits this protected join because the WHERE equality anchors it to one supplied identifier. This is a lookup for one person.
next: Now remove that one-person anchor. Try ‘Join all’ to see a different boundary.

notes: PROTECTED column patients.national_id is matched by equality through the blind index of MATCH DOMAIN person_id.
Join of PROTECTED columns medical_records.patient_national_id and patients.national_id (MATCH DOMAIN person_id) is anchored to a single protected value.

label: 4. Join all
title: Try to connect every patient to every diagnosis
sql:
SELECT p.full_name, m.diagnosis
FROM patients AS p
JOIN medical_records AS m
  ON m.patient_national_id = p.national_id;
explanation: Regular SQL links all matching records. DEP refuses the entire query with ZD107: the protected join has no one-person anchor. The boundary limits linkage, even though no ID was selected for output.
next: An approved dataset-wide join needs a declared LINKS person_id function. Releasing the IDs themselves requires DISCLOSES and REVEAL.

error.message: Join on PROTECTED columns patients.national_id and medical_records.patient_national_id is not anchored to a single protected value.
error.hint: Anchor the join with a lookup such as WHERE patients.national_id = $1, or perform it inside a function declared LINKS person_id.
